Definition: from G1487 and G1065; if indeed, seeing that, unless, (with negative) otherwise:--if (so be that, yet).
BiblicalUsage: This phrase means if indeed or seeing that, and it is if joined to the little word indeed. Paul says we shall be clothed upon if indeed we are found not naked, asks the Galatians whether they suffered so many things in vain if indeed it was in vain, and reminds the Ephesians that they heard of his stewardship if indeed they did. The phrase states a fact and builds on it, rather than doubting it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe if indeed is faith reasoning from what God has already done, because Paul builds his argument on facts his readers already know.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
